scenes.title: Kafka Producers
scenes.subtitle: Writing events into Kafka reliably
scenes.narration: A Kafka producer is the client application that publishes events into topics, balancing speed against durability.

scenes.title: What a Producer Controls
bullets: Which topic and partition each event goes to
scenes.narration: A producer decides which topic and, through keys, which partition each event targets. It sets the acknowledgement level using the acks setting, which controls how many replicas must confirm a write. It can batch and compress events to boost throughput. And it can enable retries and idempotence so that transient failures do not create duplicates.

scenes.title: Choosing an acks Level
scenes.narration: With acks equal to one, the producer waits only for the partition leader to confirm, which is fast but can lose data if that leader fails before replication. With acks equal to all, every in-sync replica must confirm, which is slower but gives the strongest durability guarantee. Most production systems favor acks all for critical data.

scenes.title: A Producer in Python
scenes.narration: This Python producer connects to a broker and configures acks all with idempotence enabled for safe, exactly-once writes to a partition. The message key user-42 ensures all events for that user land in the same partition, preserving their order. The delivery callback reports success or failure asynchronously. Finally, flush blocks until all buffered messages are actually sent.

scenes.text: Enable idempotence and use acks=all for critical data. Use meaningful keys to keep related events ordered in the same partition.
scenes.narration: As a best practice, enable idempotence and use acks all for critical data. Use meaningful keys so that related events stay ordered within the same partition.
